turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm in a dorm with just a microwave and a kettle. Is real cooking even possible?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: More than you'd think. You can steam vegetables, cook eggs, even make a mug risotto in the microwave.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Wait, eggs in a microwave? Don't they explode?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Only if they're in the shell. Scramble them in a mug, cook for thirty seconds, stir, and repeat until set.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay that's actually useful. What about something filling for

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Instant noodles with an egg and frozen peas thrown in. Pour boiling water from the kettle, cover, and wait four minutes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Frozen peas, nice. I don't have a freezer though, just a tiny fridge.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then use a tin of sweetcorn or some spinach. Spinach wilts in seconds in hot noodles.
